name: Carvedilol
class: Non-selective beta blocker with alpha-1 blockade
summary: A non-selective beta blocker with added alpha-1 blockade, one of the three beta blockers proven to reduce mortality in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF).
mechanism: Blocks beta-1, beta-2, and alpha-1 adrenergic receptors, lowering heart rate, contractility, and peripheral vascular resistance without reflex tachycardia.

dosing.adult: Heart failure: start 3.125 mg twice daily, double every 2 weeks to target 25 mg twice daily; hypertension: 6.25–12.5 mg twice daily
dosing.maxDose: 50 mg twice daily (HFrEF, >85 kg); 25 mg twice daily otherwise

contraindications: Decompensated heart failure requiring IV inotropes
warnings: Do not stop abruptly — rebound ischemia risk
Hypotension and dizziness, especially during up-titration
May worsen heart failure during titration — monitor weight and symptoms
Caution in COPD and peripheral vascular disease
monitoring: Weight and heart-failure symptoms during titration
safety.overdose: Severe bradycardia, hypotension, bronchospasm, and heart failure; treat with atropine, glucagon, and supportive care.

indications: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (NYHA II–IV)
Left ventricular dysfunction after myocardial infarction
clinicalPearls: Alpha-1 blockade gives it a vasodilating profile unique among the HFrEF beta blockers, at the cost of more orthostatic dizziness.
Taking with food slows absorption and reduces orthostatic hypotension.
good: HFrEF and hypertension with high sympathetic tone; mortality benefit in heart failure.
bad: Asthma, decompensated heart failure, or severe hepatic impairment.
